title: བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། ཚད་མ། མེ (Derge Tengyur, vol. 185)
shelf_note: Derge woodblock folio of a pramāṇa commentary (doubt arising over a post versus a man, sdong gru / skyes bu), in the Tshad ma section as catalogued.

ocr_errors.image: ཐུན་མོང་བའི་སྣང་བ་འདི་དོན་ཉིད་ཡིན་ནོ་ཞེས་པ་ལ་ལན་འདེབས་པ (as far as I can read it)
ocr_errors.problem: The opening clause appears to say the common appearance IS the object itself. The OCR inserts a negation ('is not the object') and drops ཞེས་པ་ལ, which reverses the thesis being answered. My reading of the glyph after དོན is medium-confidence.
'upright' (འགྲེང་བ) misread as 'follow' (འབྲང་བ), which makes the definition of cognition meaningless

ocr_errors.image: possibly དེ་ལྟར … རྣམ་པ … (unclear at this resolution)
ocr_errors.problem: uncertain reading of the 'cloth/vase' clause; the sense ('cloth of a post … vase-ness') is odd and may come from misreads

tr_errors_A.english: the objection that a common appearance is not the actual object
tr_errors_A.problem: Carries the OCR's inserted negation into English. Measured against the image, the thesis is reversed.

tr_errors_A.english: Because it is not the case, memory is the cause of doubt, as the universal is perceived through direct perception.
tr_errors_A.problem: the conditional 'if memory were the cause of doubt' is turned into a flat assertion that memory is the cause of doubt

tr_errors_A.english: If one asks, "Since both are not seen here now, does doubt not arise?"
tr_errors_A.problem: the opponent's assertion ('therefore there is no doubt') is rendered as a question

tr_errors_B.english: to the objection that what appears in common is not an actual object
tr_errors_B.problem: Carries the OCR's inserted negation into English. Measured against the image, the thesis is reversed.

tr_errors_B.english: Cognition is determined to follow this.
tr_errors_B.problem: Follows the misread འབྲང and gives nonsense. The sense is 'cognition is the certainty "this is upright"', and A recovers it.

tr_errors_B.english: one does not see either one of them
tr_errors_B.problem: 'one or the other is not seen' becomes 'neither is seen'
'without direct perception' is an interpretive addition that is not in the text

pages.prefer_reason: Both repeat the OCR's opening negation. A recovers 'this is upright' where B writes the nonsense 'determined to follow this', and B also turns 'one of the two is not seen' into 'neither is seen'. A's flattening of the conditional is the lesser fault.

book_verdict: A genuine Derge pramāṇa folio with a mostly sound transcription. The opening clause appears to carry an inserted negation that reverses the thesis being answered (medium confidence), and both translations repeat it. A is otherwise the more faithful English.
